title: Unexpected Behaviors for a Chain of Groups, when Groups contain failing tasks

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case Apologies for not including test cases as a PR, because I need to find a workaround quickly, but wanted to make sure you had enough to reproduce the problems I am observing, so I have included a zip of files that can be run via docker-compose to reproduce the problem, via Python unittest: [celery_bug_report.zip](https://github.com/celery/celery/files/13892045/celery_bug_report.zip) Basic gist of the problem is that I have identified several cases where the behavior of a chain of groups is not what I would anticipate when those groups may fail. I've tried to include test cases that demonstrate both functioning and failing combinations, as I do not know enough about the celery internals to speculate as to a root cause. See the test suite for all combinations, but some highlights below: Consider the following tasks.py: ```python @app.task def fail(arg): raise MockException(arg) @app.task def identity(arg): return arg class MockException(Exception): pass ``` If we have a chain of two groups, and the first group fails, the exception is not raised in the result: ``` def test_group_chain_2_fail_1(self): sig = celery.chain( celery.group( tasks.identity.si("a"), tasks.fail.si("b"), ), celery.group( tasks.identity.si("c"), tasks.identity.si("d"), ), ) result = sig.apply_async() with self.assertRaises(tasks.MockException): result.get(TIMEOUT) ``` However, if it is the second group that fails, the exception is raised as we would expect: ```python def test_group_chain_2_fail_2(self): sig = celery.chain( celery.group( tasks.identity.si("a"), tasks.identity.si("b"), ), celery.group( tasks.identity.si("c"), tasks.fail.si("d"), ), ) result = sig.apply_async() with self.assertRaises(tasks.MockException): result.get(TIMEOUT) ``` Bizarrely, if we pad the end of the chain with a normal task, then the exception is raised even if it is in the first group! ```python def test_group_chain_2_padded_fail_1(self): sig = celery.chain( celery.group( tasks.identity.si("a"), tasks.fail.si("b"), ), celery.group( tasks.identity.si("c"), tasks.identity.si("d"), ), tasks.identity.si("end"), ) result = sig.apply_async() with self.assertRaises(tasks.MockException): result.get(TIMEOUT) ``` This may indicate a potential leak somewhere in the code. If we pad the end of the chain, as above, and the second group fails, we do get an exception on `result.get()`, but it is a ChordError and not the MockException. This is potentially acceptable behavior, but it is not consistent with the behavior observed in `test_group_chain_2_fail_1`. ```python def test_group_chain_2_padded_fail_2(self): sig = celery.chain( celery.group( tasks.identity.si("a"), tasks.identity.si("b"), ), celery.group( tasks.identity.si("c"), tasks.fail.si("d"), ), tasks.identity.si("end"), ) result = sig.apply_async() with self.assertRaises(tasks.MockException): result.get(TIMEOUT) ``` Things get weirder from here on out. For example, if we have a set of 3 groups, and the middle group fails, then we observe the same problem with the `result.get()` hanging, but if we look at the worker logs, we see that the tasks from the last group are still executed, which is unexpected. ```python def test_group_chain_3_fail_2(self): sig = celery.chain( celery.group( tasks.identity.si("a"), tasks.identity.si("b"), ), celery.group( tasks.identity.si("c"), tasks.fail.si("d"), ), celery.group( tasks.identity.si("e"), tasks.identity.si("f"), ), ) result = sig.apply_async() with self.assertRaises(tasks.MockException): result.get(TIMEOUT) ``` Worker output: ``` worker_1 | [2024-01-10 18:39:54,553: INFO/MainProcess] Task tasks.identity[0874a4a4-357c-490c-baa3-8f8d95604a03] received worker_1 | [2024-01-10
